plusJournalDesc: In-depth essays, interviews and perspectives from Foster + Partners practice.
publicationsDesc: Discover books and monographs featuring Foster + Partners work.

items.pj1Title: The Architecture of Atmosphere: Designing Football Stadiums
items.pj1Summary: From community grounds to global arenas, exploring how stadium design shapes atmosphere and collective memory.
items.pj1Body: From the early piecemeal community stadium to the commercial giants constructed today, the history of football is intertwined with the history of the stadium. Angus Campbell, Deputy Head of Studio, together with Jack Morgan, explores how design can create lasting atmosphere and collective memory.
items.pj2Summary: How new materials and digital tools are transforming the next generation of skyscrapers.
items.pj2Body: Tall buildings continue to define skylines and urban identity. This essay examines how advances in materials, structure and digital design are enabling safer, more efficient and more expressive towers.
items.pj3Summary: Designing healthy, nature-connected environments that support wellbeing and productivity.
items.pj3Body: Bringing nature into the workplace is no longer a luxury but a strategic choice. We look at how biophilic design supports wellbeing, focus and collaboration in offices and mixed-use environments.
items.pj4Summary: Pioneering low-carbon and circular materials in architecture and construction.
items.pj4Body: The shift to sustainable materials is reshaping construction. We explore innovations in low-carbon concrete, mass timber and recycled systems that reduce embodied carbon without compromising performance.
items.pj5Title: Urban Mobility and the Next Generation
items.pj5Summary: How integrated transport and placemaking are redefining city movement.
items.pj5Body: Mobility and place are increasingly designed together. This piece looks at how transit hubs, shared streets and new modes are creating more liveable, connected cities.
items.pj6Summary: Using digital twins to improve delivery, operation and lifecycle performance.
items.pj6Body: Digital twins are moving from pilot to mainstream. We examine how live digital models support design coordination, construction sequencing and long-term building performance.
items.pj7Summary: Sensitive reuse and extension of historic buildings for contemporary use.
items.pj7Body: Heritage buildings carry memory and identity. We discuss principles and examples of adaptive reuse that respect history while enabling new programmes and standards.
items.pj8Summary: Designing airport infrastructure for energy efficiency and decarbonisation.
items.pj8Body: Airports are among the most energy-intensive building types. This essay explores design and engineering strategies to move towards net zero operation and resilience.
items.pj9Summary: Achieving high density without sacrificing light, space and community.
items.pj9Body: Dense cities need dense housing. We look at how careful massing, daylight and shared amenity can deliver both density and quality of life.
items.pj10Summary: Advances in lightweight structures and long-span design.
items.pj10Body: Lightweight structures allow larger spans and lower material use. We survey recent innovations in form, material and fabrication that are extending the possibilities of light construction.
items.pj11Summary: Integrating climate adaptation into urban and regional masterplans.
items.pj11Body: Masterplans must now account for flooding, heat and extreme weather. This article outlines how we embed resilience and nature-based solutions into large-scale planning.
items.pj12Summary: Creating inclusive, engaging museum environments for collections and visitors.
items.pj12Body: Museums are places of learning and encounter. We explore how architecture and curation can work together to create accessible, memorable experiences.
items.pj13Summary: How hybrid work is reshaping office design and the role of the workplace.
items.pj13Body: The pandemic accelerated lasting change in how we work. We reflect on flexible layouts, wellness and the evolving purpose of the office.
items.pj14Summary: Data-driven facade design for comfort, energy and aesthetics.
items.pj14Body: Parametric tools allow facades to respond precisely to orientation, climate and programme. We look at projects where performance and expression go hand in hand.
items.pj15Summary: Bridges, stations and networks that stitch cities together.
items.pj15Body: Infrastructure shapes how cities function and feel. This essay examines the design of transport nodes and linear systems as civic and connective place.
items.pj16Summary: Designing for disassembly, reuse and material loops.
items.pj16Body: A circular built environment demands design for disassembly and reuse. We discuss principles and case studies that reduce waste and extend material life.
items.pj17Summary: Evidence-based design for healing environments and staff welfare.
items.pj17Body: Healthcare buildings can support recovery and reduce stress. We explore how light, nature and layout contribute to outcomes for patients and staff.
items.pj18Summary: Using data and technology to improve urban management and experience.
items.pj18Body: Data can make cities more efficient and responsive. We consider how sensing, analytics and design can be combined responsibly for urban benefit.
items.pj19Summary: Breathing new life into historic structures with care and invention.
items.pj19Body: Adaptive reuse preserves embodied carbon and cultural value. We present strategies and examples where old fabric gains new use without losing its story.
items.pj20Summary: Creating clear, comfortable and efficient interchange environments.
items.pj20Body: Transport hubs are gateways and meeting points. We look at wayfinding, comfort and commercial balance in station and interchange design.
items.pj21Title: Landscape Architecture in the Urban Realm
items.pj21Summary: Integrating landscape, ecology and public space in dense cities.
items.pj21Body: Urban landscape supports biodiversity, drainage and wellbeing. This piece examines how parks, streets and rooftops can form a connected green network.
items.pj22Summary: The rise of engineered timber and its impact on form and carbon.
items.pj22Body: Mass timber offers strength, speed and carbon benefits. We survey current applications and the design opportunities of wood at scale.
items.pj23Summary: Shaping soundscapes for comfort, clarity and inclusion.
items.pj23Body: Acoustics define how we experience shared spaces. We explore material and geometry choices that support speech, focus and ambience.
items.pj24Summary: Living walls and green facades for biodiversity and wellbeing.
items.pj24Body: Vertical greenery can cool, insulate and connect people to nature. We look at planting systems, maintenance and integration into building design.
items.pj25Summary: Off-site and modular delivery for speed, quality and affordability.
items.pj25Body: Modular construction is gaining ground in housing. We discuss design for manufacture, logistics and the balance between repetition and variation.
items.pj26Summary: Public squares, libraries and halls as places of assembly and debate.
items.pj26Body: Civic buildings embody collective values. We reflect on how architecture can support participation, transparency and democratic life.
items.pj27Summary: Light as material: shaping mood, rhythm and identity.
items.pj27Body: Light defines atmosphere and wayfinding. We examine the integration of natural and artificial light in landmark and everyday spaces.
items.pj28Summary: Reconnecting cities to water through mixed-use and public realm.
items.pj28Body: Waterfronts offer unique potential for renewal. We explore flood resilience, access and programming along rivers and coasts.
items.pj29Summary: Creating campuses that support learning, research and community.
items.pj29Body: Education buildings must adapt to changing pedagogy and technology. We look at flexibility, wellbeing and identity in campus masterplanning and buildings.
items.pj30Summary: Spaces for experimentation, collaboration and breakthrough.
items.pj30Body: Innovation thrives in the right environment. We discuss how lab and research buildings can support cross-disciplinary work and serendipity.
